batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 IDs with their supplied current point forecasts unchanged. Measure controlled gaps that test transfer of recent loading failures, explore sparsely anchored solvent-response curves, and discriminate specific predicted onset decreases. Favor labels that constrain several remaining conditions through a meaningful local comparison.

choices.reason: m19 at 1/1 and 92.2 mg forecasts 13.25/25.61 mL. The 46.1 and 138.3 mg observations a595d5f1882c39914392 and 97297c71a28a2ccbdeeb differ substantially in onset but little in completion. This missing middle amount tests whether the updated model interpolates that endpoint-specific loading association.

m19 at 2/1 and 92.2 mg forecasts 18.37/34.95 mL. Outer-amount observations 6d21e9ec887b3408c612 and 906bd247e050658f99d8 measured 23.69/34.83 and 13.39/35.04. With selected 1/1, this tests both loading interpolation and transfer of the onset response across ratios.

m186 at 10/1 and 100 mg forecasts 5.52/20.28 mL. Its measured 150 mg onset remains near 5 mL in 6fa96316d53d24c2c55c, whereas recent lower-loading weak-eluent labels departed strongly. This anchors the missing middle-amount segment before selected 20/1.

m186 at 20/1 and 100 mg forecasts 6.27/20.70 mL. Matched-ratio observations 1723e818bb3500feacec and 14636dfc9018393d202e measured 8.63/20.02 at 50 mg and 5.05/21.77 at 150 mg. The middle amount distinguishes gradual onset loading dependence from a more localized departure.

m83 at 20/1 and 154.5 mg forecasts 8.03/18.21 mL. Its matched 50/1 label 2012223149ba23d26ec2 measured 16.96/33.38, with completion underpredicted by 12.55 mL at acquisition. This locates whether the missing completion growth is already present at 20/1.

m83 at 20/1 and 51.5 mg forecasts 8.54/17.82 mL, close to the selected 154.5 mg forecast. The matched-ratio amount contrast separates loading association from solvent-response curvature; measured 103 mg 10/1 anchor 5dfa7a7352e7a66c29e6 provides an additional reference without assuming amount invariance.

m37 at 5/1 and 67.25 mg forecasts 13.08/29.19 mL. Recent matched 20/1 observation 606886b17304ec494aa0 measured 53.14/97.19 and exposed another substantial onset underprediction. Together with measured 10/1 anchor 9ae9c8b491a04e429a11, this tests how early the loading-associated onset separation appears.

m37 at 5/1 and 201.75 mg forecasts 12.53/29.48 mL. It matches the selected lower amount in solvent and injection volume, with measured middle-loading 5/1 anchor 9de8f9fed06ef9d5befa. The pair tests whether the strong loading association seen at 20/1 is already detectable at 5/1.

m108 at 20/1 and 50 mg forecasts 11.85/17.10 mL. Its matched 10/1 observation 75f1650706d11848a73a measured 7.48/13.15. Selected 20/1 and 50/1 establish a missing late response segment for a bromodimethoxy aromatic ether, where CW coverage distance is also high.

m108 at 50/1 and 50 mg forecasts 18.68/27.24 mL. With selected 20/1 and measured 10/1 anchor 75f1650706d11848a73a, it tests whether the proposed moderate extension is supported. Its crossed V2 quantiles are a calibration concern, not evidence of a measured error or calibrated uncertainty.

m122 at 20/1 and 72.25 mg forecasts 11.22/19.38 mL. Only the stronger-eluent anchor 38c7016974af225a3cde is measured for this loading. The selected 20/1–50/1 pair tests transfer between positional bromodimethoxy environments while retaining the different recorded amounts of the m108 comparison.

m122 at 50/1 and 72.25 mg forecasts 17.02/28.02 mL. This high-CW-distance extension complements selected 20/1 and measured 1/1 anchor 38c7016974af225a3cde. It distinguishes a moderate response from the much steeper measured m116 curve and the shallower m123 curve.

m111 at 10/1 and 71.2 mg forecasts 6.28/10.74 mL. Measured record d17718dc009389d217a2 anchors 20/1 at a higher amount, leaving the lower-loading curve sparse. This supplies an internal anchor for selected 50/1 rather than relying entirely on related anisole structures.

m111 at 50/1 and 71.2 mg forecasts 7.14/14.27 mL. The selected matched 10/1 label tests its proposed shallow extension. Comparison with measured bromomethoxy compound 18d862fb465d82320e1e can teach structural differences in onset and completion without attributing them solely to methyl substitution or ignoring loading differences.

m109 at 50/1 and 79.5 mg forecasts 8.25/16.09 mL. Matched 20/1 observation 97f693e8a82af54da0ed measured 6.30/11.26. This adds an uncovered weak-eluent extension in a fluoro/bromo anisole environment connected to the selected mono- and dimethoxy panels.

m184 at 20/1 and 100 mg forecasts 5.01/13.34 mL, slightly below the measured 10/1 completion of 13.80 in e78030609295a056f86f. With selected 50/1, it tests whether the proposed shallow completion curve and local decrease are real for the sterically crowded aldehyde.

m184 at 50/1 and 100 mg forecasts 4.71/15.80 mL. The matched 10/1 anchor e78030609295a056f86f and selected 20/1 constrain the complete late segment. This tests a much shallower proposed extension than measured for several other halogenated aldehydes.

m64 at 1/1 and 138.41 mg forecasts 5.57/10.36 mL. Its supplied measured anchor 05c8e4d5f25c1295f231 is at 50/1, so the strong-eluent baseline remains uncovered. The selected 1/1–10/1 pair directly tests a forecast onset decrease in an aryl propyl-ketone environment.

m64 at 10/1 matches selected 1/1 and forecasts 3.46/13.23 mL. This onset decline is untested; measured 50/1 record 05c8e4d5f25c1295f231 has onset 6.47 mL. The pair can distinguish a genuine early minimum from the interpolation failures recently found in other neutral carbonyl compounds.

m169 at 20/1 and 122 mg forecasts 6.30/22.72 mL. Matched observations 9b11493847c035abf800 at 10/1 and f46da3c00b2199795e4c at 50/1 measured 6.27/17.48 and 6.78/36.16. This fills a high-CW-distance gap and tests completion growth independently of its nearly flat onset.

m203 at 1/1 and 50 mg forecasts 4.92/7.77 mL, below the selected pure-EA forecast in onset. Measuring both establishes a missing strong-eluent response segment and distinguishes a real local decrease from baseline miscalibration before the measured 5/1 anchor 5885d427a26f03e522f3.

m73 at 10/1 matches the selected pure-EA loading conditions and forecasts 5.70/15.28 mL. The pair tests the model's proposed onset decline and whether anomalous strong-eluent behavior extends into an ordered response curve. Nearby-density measured record 77f65db1224c7c295678 is a reference, not an exact condition match.

m164 at 5/1 and 104.77 mg forecasts 4.78/19.35 mL. Matched 1/1 and 10/1 observations 3f6b817d855e67b3b406 and 7726f4a207a737256a86 were 5.13/10.05 and 6.34/20.41. This tests a rapid early completion increase followed by a shallow segment, complementing the selected chalcone curve.

m167 at 5/1 matches selected 2/1 and forecasts 3.06/14.84 mL, versus measured 10/1 onset 4.83 in 25dd969086d07da70d74. The controlled pair distinguishes a genuine early dip from another onset interpolation artifact while separately measuring completion growth.

hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on both compound and ratio and can affect onset much more than completion. m19 shows a large onset association at 1/1–2/1; m186's weak-eluent onset plateau does not transfer to the lower amount. Nitro-carbonyl examples show additional endpoint-specific associations. Missing amounts and earlier ratios may still be inadequately represented.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled loading contrasts can teach separate V1 and V2 responses and compound–ratio–loading interactions that transfer beyond individual acquired points.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do middle-loading m19 and m186 labels interpolate the outer amounts, and do m37, m193, m88 and m90 show loading-associated onset differences at their selected earlier ratios?

hypotheses.content: m83's measured 154.5 mg 50/1 completion rejected its shallow acquisition forecast. It remains unresolved whether the departure reflects a later solvent-response knee, an amount association, or both. m97's steep late extension transferred to the lower amount, but that does not establish a shared ester response curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched 20/1 amount contrast plus the existing higher-loading 50/1 label separates solvent curvature from loading transfer within an ester family.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m83 completion already substantially above its approximately 18 mL forecast at 20/1, and does the answer differ between 51.5 and 154.5 mg?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic ether response curves require structural context: measured m116 and m123 extensions differ markedly. The predicted moderate weak-eluent extensions of m108 and m122, and shallow extensions of m111 and m109, remain untested. Methoxy arrangement, other substituents and their structural environments are plausible contributors, not established explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These sparsely anchored molecules have many remaining condition rows. Connected response segments can teach transferable structural distinctions while improving coverage of the current gradient feature space.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the bromodimethoxy compounds follow their proposed moderate 20/1–50/1 extensions, and do the selected monomethoxy compounds retain their predicted shallow onset responses?

hypotheses.content: The two ortho bromines in m184 could reduce accessibility of its aldehyde interaction with silica, making a shallow late response chemically plausible. However, the predicted 10/1–20/1 completion decrease and very modest 50/1 extension have no measured confirmation. Other measured halogenated aldehydes have distinct late completion curves.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched late segment tests whether steric context supports a genuinely shallow curve or whether the model is underestimating an uncovered aldehyde response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m184 completion remain near 13–16 mL through 20/1–50/1, or does substantial growth appear despite its crowded carbonyl environment?

hypotheses.content: Predicted onset decreases require local experimental discrimination. Recent m131 and m176 middle-ratio depressions failed, while m80 had a genuine measured local decline. The current m64 1/1–10/1, m203 pure-EA–1/1 and m167 2/1–5/1 decreases are untested and should not be accepted or rejected through a universal monotonicity rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched pairs distinguish real curvature from interpolation artifacts across several chemical environments and constrain onset separately from completion.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which, if any, of the three selected onset decreases survive measurement, and how does completion change over each same-loading segment?

hypotheses.content: m164 and m165 have different measured 20/1 onset baselines despite related conjugated aromatic ketone structures. Their missing earlier segments may also differ: m164 is forecast to complete most of its early increase by 5/1, while m165 is forecast to show continuing completion growth with little onset change.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The connected panel tests whether conjugation and carbonyl environment change endpoint coupling and response shape rather than merely shifting a common curve.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m164's 5/1 completion already approach its measured 10/1 value, and does m165 maintain a shallow onset across its newly measured 2/1–10/1 segment?

hypotheses.content: m73's conflicting strong-eluent records may reflect variability or behavior not resolved by the recorded inputs. They do not establish a physical discontinuity from the tiny density difference between 1.049 and 1.0491. The elevated pure-EA forecast at a new amount may represent propagation of anomalous records rather than a transferable solvent response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A new amount with matched pure-EA and 10/1 labels tests transfer beyond conflicting tuples and can limit inappropriate density sensitivity, while acknowledging potentially irreducible variation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the higher-loading pure-EA onset remain elevated relative to 10/1, or does it return to the approximately 4–5 mL baseline seen in several measured records?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measurements sharpen several earlier hypotheses. m211's 10/1 completions are close across amounts: 30.88, 31.50 and 32.11 mL, whereas its measured outer-amount 50/1 completions differ by over 21 mL. This supports a ratio-dependent loading association and reduces the immediate value of another early m211 condition. m97's steep extension transferred to the lower amount, with 32.07/47.81 mL at 50/1; m101's new extension was also much closer to its acquisition forecasts. In contrast, m83's 50/1 completion was underpredicted by 12.55 mL at acquisition, motivating its controlled 20/1 contrast. The proposed deep m131 and m176 onset depressions failed: their new 20/1 onsets were 5.18 and 4.72 mL. Those curves are now sufficiently anchored to defer further immediate extensions. m33's new outer-amount 50/1 labels both retained early onset, but completion was 26.73 mL at the lower amount and 39.01 mL at the higher amount; the middle amount had a later onset than either outer amount, so a simple monotonic onset-loading rule is unsupported. m80 recovered at lower-loading 50/1 after its measured 10/1–20/1 decline. m62's lower-loading 2/1 label exceeded its 1/1 endpoints, rejecting the proposed lower-loading early minimum. Their remaining errors and gaps are less compelling than the selected uncovered relationships. The clearest new loading-transfer failure was m186: its lower-loading onset rose from 8.63 at 20/1 to 13.49 mL at 50/1, unlike the approximately 5 mL higher-loading plateau. m19 likewise revealed large onset differences between outer amounts with nearly equal completion, and m37's lower-loading 20/1 onset remained substantially underpredicted. These outcomes motivate missing-amount and earlier-ratio tests. m197's interpolation and m117's lower-loading 5/1 result add useful anchors without resolving m117's anomalous middle-loading 10/1 record. m143's new completion labels exceeded its acquisition forecasts, while m187 retained shallow onset and later completion growth. These distinct aldehyde curves motivate testing the still-sparse crowded m184 extension. All error statements here refer to acquisition-time forecasts, not current-model residuals. Evidence attribution follows the observed table, including c6924324ddd95f249df6 as m107 rather than the inherited m26 description.
batch_rationale: The batch combines recent failure transfer with exploration of relationships that remain weakly anchored across the supplied pool. The loading experiments distinguish onset associations from completion associations and test when they emerge along a solvent-response curve. The aromatic ether panel covers several molecules with many remaining conditions and creates interpretable local segments around measured anchors; high CW distances support its coverage value, but structural questions drive the choices. The m184, m64, m169 and conjugated-ketone experiments expand response-shape coverage where borrowing from related carbonyl compounds leaves competing possibilities. The m203 and m167 pairs audit specific onset decreases, informed by both rejected minima and genuine measured declines elsewhere. The m73 pair tests whether an anomalous strong-eluent pattern transfers to a new amount without treating conflicting records as a mechanism. All selected molecule-plus-condition tuples are distinct, and the batch avoids redundant aliases. Already repaired m80, m62, m131 and m176 segments receive no further immediate measurements. Cross-molecule comparisons retain differences in loading amount, solvent and loading-solvent volume. This design may improve Row-distribution generalization by teaching baselines, local curvature, endpoint coupling and structure–condition–loading interactions. Quantile spans are uncalibrated single-predictor outputs, CW distance measures feature-space coverage, and V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width; none is used as a mandatory acquisition score or interpreted as epistemic uncertainty.
